chunks: He [al-Mufid] said: Abu Ubayd Allah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki reported to us, saying: Abu al-Ayna narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, from Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Ka'b, from Mujahid, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, said:

Renounce this world, which no one before you has ever fully enjoyed, and which will not remain for anyone after you. Your path in it is the path of those who have passed before you. It has withered and announced its end. Its familiar face has turned strange, informing its inhabitants of annihilation and its dwellers of death.

What was once sweet in it has turned bitter, and what was once clear has become murky. Nothing remains of it except a residue like the dregs at the bottom of a waterskin, or a sip like the last drop in a vessel—if the thirsty one were to suckle it, it would not quench his thirst.

So resolve firmly to depart from this abode whose inhabitants are destined for decline, whose people are denied the continuation of life, and whose souls are humbled by death. No living being can hope for permanence, and no soul but is submissive before mortality. Let not hopes delude you, nor let the passage of time lull you, and do not be deceived by its false promises.

Even if you were to moan with the longing of a bereft camel, and call out like the cooing of doves, and cry out with the wailing of devoted monks, and go forth to God Most High renouncing wealth and children, seeking nearness to Him through the elevation of a rank before Him or the forgiveness of a sin recorded by His scribes and preserved by His angels—all of that would still be little compared to what I hope for you of His reward and what I fear for you of His punishment.
May God make us and you among the repentant worshippers.

key_terms.ازهدوا: renounce - turn away from worldly attachment
key_terms.التائبين العابدين: repentant worshippers - those who return to God in devotion
key_terms.الفناء: annihilation - total destruction of the world

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about renouncing the world and preparing for the afterlife?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib exhorts renunciation of the transient world, which has withered and announced its end. He warns that even the most extreme devotion would be little compared to God's reward and punishment, and prays that God makes us among the repentant worshippers.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki, who reported from Abu al-Ayna, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, from Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Ka’b, from Mujahid who reported that: Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, said:

"Be least interested in this world from which no one from your predecessors ever benefited, nor will it remain for anyone after you have gone! The path you are walking on is the same as that of the bygones, totally cut off and subjected to annihilations, their good deeds forgotten and unknown. This world warns its inmates of destruction, and its residents of Death.

That which was once sweet from it has become bitter; and that which was once clear has become turbid. Nothing has ever remained in it except like the last droplets of water in a vessel, or a few gulps, which if a thirsty were to suck up, would not be satiated.

So, be prepared for a journey from this abode, whose residents are destined to perish, and prevented from living forever. They have been submitted to dying, therefore no life should crave perpetuity. Everyone here awaits death. Let no hopes and expectations digress you, nor should you regard it as a long age; and do not be deceived by its promises.

And, if you were to roam about like a camel yearning to find its heifer and coo like a dove, calling its young one, and raise your beseeching cry like a worshipful hermit, and come out together with your wealth and children, so as to seek nearness to Him, and be elevated in His estimation; or to be forgiven the sins which His angels and scribes have recorded, it would all be too little to earn His reward which I hope for you, or to be saved from His wrath which I fear for you.
May Allah keep us and you among the repentents and the worshipping ones."
